t: Pick the database for the booking service
ctx: Bookings grow about 20% a month, and the prototype's single SQLite file starts failing writes under load.
explain:
The booking service still runs on the SQLite file the prototype started with. It is fine for reads, but concurrent writes queue up and start failing once about fifty land at once, which already happens on Friday evenings.

All three routes fix Friday. They differ in how much work it is now, and how long until you have to think about it again.

In short: move to managed Postgres this week, jump to distributed SQL for multi-region, or patch SQLite and decide later.

opts.label: Managed Postgres
opts.note: Boring and proven, backups built in. About a day to migrate.
opts.p: Move the booking service to managed Postgres this week. Plan the migration, keep SQLite read-only as a fallback for 7 days, then retire it.

opts.label: Distributed SQL
opts.note: Multi-region from day one. Newer tooling, harder to debug.
opts.p: Move the booking service to a distributed SQL database now, with a multi-region setup. Write up the operational runbook before cutover.

opts.label: Stay on SQLite for now
opts.note: Turn on WAL mode and queue writes. Revisit at 10k bookings a day.
opts.p: Keep SQLite: enable WAL mode, put writes behind a queue, and add an alert at 10k bookings a day so we revisit the database then.

ctx: v2 is feature-complete and behind a flag. The load test finishes next Friday.
explain:
v2 is done and hidden behind a feature flag, so launching is just a question of who gets it when. The only open risk is load: the full test finishes next Friday.

A staged rollout gets real traffic early while keeping any problem small. Everything can be switched off in under a minute.

In short: roll out 10% → 50% → 100% this week, give it to everyone on Monday, or wait for the load test.

opts.label: Staged, starting Monday
opts.note: 10% Monday, 50% Wednesday, everyone Friday if error rates stay flat.
opts.p: Launch v2 as a staged rollout: 10% Monday, 50% Wednesday, 100% Friday, each step only if error rates stay flat. Owner watches the dashboard at each step.

opts.label: Everyone on Monday
opts.note: Fastest feedback. If something breaks, it breaks for everybody.
opts.p: Launch v2 to everyone on Monday. Keep the flag ready to switch off, and have the on-call engineer watch error rates all day.

opts.label: Wait for the load test
opts.note: Launch a week later, with the load numbers in hand.
opts.p: Hold v2 until the load test finishes next Friday, then launch the following Monday with a staged rollout.

ctx: Three customers used it last month; 412 used the new export. It blocks the reporting refactor.
explain:
The old CSV export still works, but three customers used it last month against 412 on the new one. Keeping it means the reporting refactor has to work around it.

It is low stakes either way, so there is no recommendation: this is a judgement call about those three customers.

In short: remove it next release after emailing them, remove it today, or hide it and live with the extra code.
